clue.text: One who cracks up?

parts.note: reads like someone who laughs a lot, but means a thief who climbs up buildings to crack safes and break in

explanation.definitionFit: A housebreaker who climbs walls and drainpipes to get in through upper windows, then cracks safes.

clue.text: Cabbage king

explanation.surface: A monarch who is a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Cole is an old name for cabbage and kale; Old King Cole is the merry old soul of the nursery rhyme.

clue.text: Hybrid fruit of strong flavour the Spanish love

parts.note: a tang is a sharp, strong taste
el is Spanish for 'the'
love is nil in tennis scoring, written as O

explanation.surface: A cross-bred fruit with a strong taste that people in Spain adore.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangelo is a citrus cross between a tangerine and a pomelo or grapefruit.

clue.text: An album of the new style is incomprehensible

indicators.note: the letters are recast in a new form, a fresh style of arrangement

explanation.surface: A critic finds a record in some new musical fashion impossible to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of the new style' reads as describing the album, but 'of the' is fodder too: AN ALBUM OF THE is rearranged, with 'new style' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that cannot be fathomed, i.e. whose depths cannot be measured, is beyond understanding.

clue.text: After semi-gybe, the ordinary sailor is going round in circles!

indicators.note: the sailor comes after the half-gybe, placing those letters second
semi- means half, so only the first half of the word gybe is used

parts.note: a rating is a sailor in the navy without a commission

explanation.surface: A sailor, after half-completing a gybe, ends up turning round in circles.
explanation.walkthrough: A gybe is a sailing manoeuvre swinging the sail across; half of GYBE is GY.
explanation.definitionFit: To gyrate is to whirl or spin about a central point.

clue.text: Euterpe, for example, died delighted

parts.note: Euterpe is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, the Muse of music
d is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Euterpe died, and someone was pleased about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Amused and delighted both describe being entertained and pleased.

clue.text: Daughter to Lincoln, retired

indicators.note: to here means added on to, so the daughter's letter is attached to the end

parts.note: Abe is the familiar name of Abraham Lincoln

explanation.surface: Lincoln's daughter has gone into retirement.
explanation.definitionFit: Retired in the sense of gone to bed for the night, so lying in bed.

clue.text: Excellent piece of play in Dublin- Derry meeting

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the run of letters of the two city names

explanation.surface: A brilliant passage of play in a sports match between Dublin and Derry.
explanation.definitionFit: In British sporting slang a blinder is an outstanding performance or shot.

clue.text: Girl with short skirt to take off is degraded

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
a mini is a very short skirt
to shed is to take off or cast off, as with clothes or skin

explanation.surface: A girl with a miniskirt removing it is humiliated.
explanation.definitionFit: Diminished means lessened in status or dignity, so brought low.

clue.text: Wool-bearing sea lion fur? That is crazy!

indicators.note: crazy means wild or disordered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sea lion with woolly fur? That would be mad!
explanation.definitionFit: Laniferous comes from Latin lana, wool, plus -ferous, carrying: producing fleece.

clue.text: Steady business

explanation.surface: A reliable company.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm means stable and fixed; a firm is also a company or commercial enterprise.

clue.text: Theatrical backer, a civvy serving the military

parts.note: camp means exaggeratedly theatrical
a follower is a supporter or backer

explanation.surface: A theatre's financial backer is a civilian working for the army.
explanation.definitionFit: A civilian who travels with an army to sell goods or services to soldiers.

clue.text: Temporary cover for red wine

explanation.surface: A wine that briefly shelters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tent is a portable canvas shelter; tent is also a deep red Spanish wine used as communion wine.

clue.text: Septimus Harding starting to cut wood

indicators.note: starting means only the first letter of the word to is taken

parts.note: to hew is to cut with an axe
Arden is the forest in Shakespeare's As You Like It and a real Warwickshire woodland

explanation.surface: A man named Septimus Harding begins chopping timber.
explanation.walkthrough: Septimus Harding is the title character of Anthony Trollope's novel; 'Harding starting' tempts you to take H, but 'starting' acts on 'to'.
explanation.definitionFit: Septimus Harding is the hospital warden who is the title role in Trollope's novel, the first Barsetshire book.

clue.text: Booty left at sea in a wet blanket?

parts.note: spoils are plunder or booty taken in war
on a ship, port is the left-hand side

explanation.surface: Pirate loot left at sea wrapped in a soggy blanket.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet blanket is someone who dampens others' fun, a killjoy.

clue.text: Intellectual head of faculty university don, it turns out

parts.note: a prof, short for professor, heads a university faculty

indicators.note: turns out suggests the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A faculty head and a university don prove to be clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Profound means having deep insight or great learning.

clue.text: Things that serve to animate young men

explanation.surface: What enlivens a group of lads.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparks ignite and enliven things; sparks is also an old word for lively, showy young fellows.

clue.text: Old aircraft to run lightly over path

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: to trip is to move with light, quick steps
a lane is a narrow path or road

explanation.surface: Someone skips nimbly across a track past a vintage plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A triplane, with three wings stacked, is an early aeroplane design, like the Fokker Dr.I.

clue.text: Book a first-class return during his trip?

indicators.note: during means the following letters fall within those of the other piece
a trip means a stumble, so the letters of his are knocked out of order
return means the first-class letters are read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: He books a first-class return ticket for his journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his trip' reads as the prophet's journey, but 'trip' is the anagram signal for 'his', and 'return' turns only the first-class letters; 'during' puts the A and turned letters inside the jumbled word.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaiah is a prophetic book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: One encourages a punter

parts.note: a punter is a gambler, one who places a bet

explanation.surface: Someone encouraging a gambler.
explanation.definitionFit: An abetter is someone who supports or eggs on another, often in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Appropriate for Yorkshire spa not to open

indicators.note: not to open means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: Harrogate is a spa town in North Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: Is it fitting for a Yorkshire spa to stay closed?
explanation.definitionFit: To arrogate is to claim or seize something without right, a verb sense of appropriate.

clue.text: All birds brown in ancient Iranian language?

parts.note: Aves is the zoological class that includes all birds
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: Every bird is brown in some old Persian tongue?
explanation.definitionFit: Avestan is the old Iranian tongue of the Zoroastrian scriptures, the Avesta.

clue.text: Devastating constraint at one time on Henry V?

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: let is an archaic word for a hindrance, surviving in 'without let or hindrance'
Prince Hal is Shakespeare's name for the young Henry V

explanation.surface: A crushing restriction once placed on King Henry V?
explanation.definitionFit: Lethal means deadly, causing destruction.

clue.text: Hull to accumulate such a lot of domestic rubbish?

parts.note: a hull is an outer husk or shell, as of a seed
to heap is to pile up or amass

explanation.surface: The city of Hull piling up an awful lot of household waste.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull looks like the English city, but it means a husk.
explanation.definitionFit: A shell heap is a prehistoric midden of discarded shells and household refuse.

clue.text: Wolf song invented?

explanation.surface: A wolf's howl that was made up?
explanation.definitionFit: Hugo Wolf composed German art songs called Lieder; lied also means told untruths, made things up.

clue.text: Small ones may be carried in them

definitions.text: Small ones may be carried in them

parts.words: Small ones may be carried in them
parts.note: babies are carried in the limbs, and small weapons such as pistols are a kind of these, a pun on ...

explanation.definitionFit: Small arms are handguns and rifles, and a small child is carried in your upper limbs.

clue.text: Something sworn at in cry of pain

indicators.note: in means the word at is put inside the cry

parts.note: oh is an exclamation of pain or surprise

explanation.surface: Someone swears at another while crying out in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A solemn vow or pledge is sworn; an oath can also be a curse.

clue.text: Low flier where a tar's at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A bird skims low where a sailor is out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Shearwaters are seabirds that glide low over the waves, almost touching them.

clue.text: Directed, we hear, in breach of duty

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is said aloud and sounds like the answer

parts.note: taught in the sense of instructed or directed

explanation.surface: Someone instructed, so we're told, in a failure of obligation.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the two words sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a tort is a civil wrong, a breach of a duty owed to another.

clue.text: Sketches for naughty pictures

parts.note: blue means risqué or smutty, as in blue films
prints are photographic pictures or engravings

explanation.surface: Drawings intended for rude photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: Blueprints are technical plans or design drawings.
